summary: Interpretation recorded for the view-lag question (CheckRun 0adb78b8f8da429f865c2abb097b4ff8, exit 0). All six comparisons are complete and hold: across three runs every one of the twelve node observations reflected the committed DemoteVoter transition within 0-20ms, and no node's view was stale at a sample where its own LastIndex had already reached the configuration entry (stale_max_last_index never above 2 against configuration index 3), so the only stale samples predate the entry's arrival. Conclusion holds; the scoped defect claim is refuted: with the source path showing a peer's view is written when the entry is newly appended (or installed with a snapshot), and every log having reached index 3, a multi-second view lag does not occur on a healthy cluster in this construction. The question is closed with boundaries kept explicit - lightweight healthy conditions only, four runs total, and the single sighting that opened it (index 0 of the extended-window receipt) remains unidentified rather than explained. A durable fact was promoted for the convergence behaviour, and in the same submission I asked for a repeat of the fixed extended-window experiment, which gives an independent sample of the lease-window result and re-samples the near_node_self_voter field from the original harness that produced the unexplained sighting.
